text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- 2,000 teachers from 66 schools in five counties participated in a warning strike yesterday over pay issues in the first teachers' strike to hit Estonia.
- Visiting Euro-commissioner Martin Bannemann met prime minister Mart Siimann and other government members; Bannemann applauded Estonia's progress in developing info-technology.
- The Arno Tali Foundation delivered 25 stipends of 2,000 kroons each to young people from rural areas at a ceremony in Tallinn Town Hall on Monday.
- Liberal humanism was the basis for a welfare state, the chairwoman of the Finnish parliament Riitta Uosukainen said in her speech at Tartu University yesterday.
- The enterprise commission for the Tartu government recommends selling the town's department store to Atterost, a commission member said.
- Lightning hit a house in Viljandi county; the damage by the resulting fire was slight but the framework of the building was dislodged. Nobody was injured.
- The interior ministers of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania formed a group to coordinate drug-fighting and signed a cooperation protocol at a meeting in Tallinn.
- The new mayor of Tallinn, Ivi Eenmaa, decided to keep the former city government in office.
- Neeme Jogi, the secretary general to the Coalition Party, said he would leave politics for the private sector.
- Protective customs tariffs might damage Estonia's liberal economic reputation, Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves said in parliament, answering MP Mart Laar's question about this possibility.
